questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Release Automation?
options: Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
Release automation validates a version/ref, generates notes or assets, applies scoped publication permissions, and keeps the release traceable to source.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
questions.answer_key: Release automation validates a version/ref, generates notes or assets, applies scoped publication permissions, and keeps the release traceable to source.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of release automation: Release automation validates a version/ref, generates notes or assets, applies scoped publication permissions, and keeps the release traceable to source. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.explanation: Version tagging: Use filters to reduce unnecessary runs only when skipped work is genuinely unrelated. questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to release automation?
options: Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: Release automation validates a version/ref, generates notes or assets, applies scoped publication permissions, and keeps the release traceable to source. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
